Build a five-nearest-neighbor router using frozen Contriever embeddings and neighbors' per-model correctness, while selecting global and task-conditioned fixed-model baselines using validation data only. Report held-out macroaccuracy, the fraction solved by only one candidate, and stratified paired bootstrap intervals, with an oracle selecting among cached outputs reported only as a diagnostic.

follow_ups.title: Predicting cost before model selection
follow_ups.question: Does predicting model-dependent output length improve cost-aware routing over input-length-only estimates?
follow_ups.method: Generate local, batched, deterministic responses from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on 192 GSM8K questions split 96/32/64 into training/validation/test sets, with 192-token caps and recorded input/output tokens and GPU time. Hold five-nearest-neighbor quality estimates from frozen Contriever embeddings constant while routing by predicted quality minus weighted estimated cost, comparing input-only cost with input plus neighbor-predicted output length; use Table 9 tariffs strictly as hypothetical prices, not actual local charges. Tune trade-off weights for three mean-budget targets spanning the fixed policies' validation costs, then report achieved test quality, cost-prediction error, budget overruns and paired uncertainty against both fixed policies.

follow_ups.title: Decomposer versus aggregator bottlenecks
follow_ups.question: How do decomposer capacity and aggregator capacity separately affect multiround quality?
follow_ups.method: On 48 held-out GSM8K questions, locally use Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct or Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct independently as decomposer and aggregator in a 2-by-2 factorial experiment, while every specialist call uses the 7B model. Adapt Appendix F to at most two subquestions, cap decomposition at 96 tokens, specialists at 128 and final/direct answers at 192, and reuse each decomposition's specialist replies across aggregator conditions. Compare deterministic answer accuracy and fully counted trajectory tokens with direct 3B and 7B answers, using paired question-level intervals to estimate the two stage effects and their interaction.

follow_ups.title: Selective continuation after a first answer
follow_ups.question: Can a learned sufficiency gate improve the quality-cost frontier relative to always decomposing?
follow_ups.method: For 100 GSM8K questions, locally cache Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct first answers, direct Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct answers, and continuations using 3B decomposition, at most two 7B specialist calls, and 3B aggregation of the draft and specialist replies, with respective 96/128/192-token caps and 192-token direct-answer caps. Using frozen Contriever query-plus-draft embeddings, train a five-nearest-neighbor predictor of the accuracy gain from continuing on 40 questions, tune stopping thresholds on 20, and evaluate 40 others where the gate sees only the query and first draft. Compare accuracy versus total trajectory tokens with never continuing, always continuing, direct 7B answering and random continuation at matched continuation rates, charging cached calls their original token costs and reporting paired intervals.

follow_ups.title: Answer-alphabet restrictions as an evaluation confound
follow_ups.question: Do the appendix's restricted answer alphabets distort direct-versus-multiround comparisons on ten-option questions?
follow_ups.method: Take 60 MMLU-Pro test questions with six gold answers per letter A-J, and locally run direct Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct answers plus two-subquestion 7B specialists followed by 3B aggregation. Retain all ten options and compare only Appendix F's printed A-D direct-answer and A-E aggregation restrictions with task-correct A-J restrictions, reusing identical decompositions and specialist replies across aggregation variants. Use one format-insensitive final-letter parser and report accuracy, parse failures and instruction-alphabet violations by gold group A-D, E and F-J, with paired intervals, 96-token decomposition/specialist caps and 32-token final-answer caps.

follow_ups.title: Native images versus shared captions
follow_ups.question: How much does shared image captioning change routing headroom relative to native image processing?
follow_ups.method: On 80 multiple-choice MathVista questions, locally run Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with images limited to 512 pixels on the longest side and 32-token answer caps. Compare original image-plus-question inputs with text-only inputs containing one question-blind caption produced by the 3B model using Appendix F's caption prompt and a 160-token cap. Select each regime's fixed-model baseline on 20 calibration questions, then report accuracy, diagnostic oracle headroom, model-winner/tie changes and paired intervals on the remaining 60, charging one caption plus the selected answer in the text pipeline and recording tokens and GPU time.

follow_ups.title: Retrieval coverage versus model choice in memory
follow_ups.question: Are memory-track routing opportunities constrained more by retrieval coverage or by models' use of available evidence?
follow_ups.method: Select 80 answerable LoCoMo questions whose annotated support fits 1,024 tokens, and construct top-five Contriever, annotated-support-plus-non-support-fillers, and non-support-only contexts from the same conversation, retaining speaker/date information and applying the same context cap. Locally generate 32-token answers with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for every condition, selecting fixed baselines on 20 questions from calibration conversations and evaluating 60 questions from different conversations. Report token-level F1, annotated-support recall and fixed-versus-oracle headroom with conversation-clustered intervals, marking annotation-conditioned contexts as diagnostic rather than deployable and recording retrieval overhead.

follow_ups.title: Persona feedback versus judge and identity artifacts
follow_ups.question: Do synthetic personalization gains require persistent persona-specific feedback after controlling answer-order bias and global preferences?
follow_ups.method: Locally generate 128-token responses from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 for 60 MT-Bench first-turn questions, then have Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct judge each pair under the ten Figure 10 personas and a no-persona control in both answer orders, with eight-token judgment caps and no persona supplied to candidates. Using frozen Contriever question embeddings and a 40/20 question-disjoint training/test split, compare five-nearest-neighbor preference predictors using persistent persona IDs, pooled feedback without IDs, or independently shuffled IDs within each question. Report held-out win/tie scores, persona-induced preference changes, order agreement and invalid-judgment rates with question-clustered intervals, treating any gains as evidence about this synthetic judge rather than real-user personalization.

follow_ups.title: Node-prompt transfer with model-mix controls
follow_ups.question: Does per-node routing help beyond changing the model mix, and does orchestration boilerplate interfere with transfer?
follow_ups.method: Locally collect 32-token single-shot responses from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on an 80/20/40 training/validation/test split of ARC-Challenge and build a five-nearest-neighbor router from frozen Contriever embeddings and training correctness. Run the paper's three-agent Chain plus shared final node on test questions, comparing routing from full node prompts with routing after stripping only fixed role boilerplate from the router input; selected models always receive unchanged full prompts, with 96-token intermediate and 32-token final caps. Compare end-to-end accuracy and trajectory tokens against the fixed-model chain selected on validation data and one seeded random assignment per question matched to each policy's model counts, reporting route changes and paired intervals.

follow_ups.title: Caption value and numeric truncation in TimeSeries
follow_ups.question: Do shared chart captions change routing headroom, and do they recover information lost by numeric-input truncation?
follow_ups.method: Take up to eight TSRBench questions per listed reasoning skill whose input series each contain at most 512 values, reserve one quarter per skill for calibration, and locally generate question-blind captions with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct using full-series 512-pixel charts and 128-token caption caps. Run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with 32-token answer caps on full numeric inputs, first-200-value inputs, first-200 inputs plus correct captions, and first-200 inputs plus approximately length-matched shuffled captions, preserving questions and complete option lists. Select fixed baselines using calibration questions only and report held-out accuracy, diagnostic oracle headroom and model-winner/tie changes with paired intervals, separating series of at most 200 values from longer series and including caption-generation costs wherever captions are used.

follow_ups.title: Can a two-model query router beat fixed baselines?
follow_ups.question: On a small replication of the paper’s mixed text tasks, does query-specific selection between 3B and 7B models improve held-out accuracy over using either model for every query?
follow_ups.method: With seed 42, take 60 questions each from MMLU and GSM8K, split each task into 40 router-training and 20 held-out questions before response collection, and run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct locally using the paper’s prompts, greedy decoding, and a 256-token output cap. Fit a TF-IDF/L2-logistic selector on per-query correctness labels, breaking ties toward 3B, then compare held-out task accuracy and per-query A100 generation latency with the training-set-best fixed model and a per-query oracle.

follow_ups.title: Does task identity or query wording drive routing?
follow_ups.question: Is routing signal explained by knowing the benchmark task, or does question text add useful within-task information?
follow_ups.method: On seed-42 samples of 60 MMLU and 60 GSM8K questions, reserve 40 per task for training and 20 for testing, then run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct locally with identical greedy prompts and a 256-token cap. Fit L2-logistic selectors using task ID only, TF-IDF question text only, or both, labeling training items by the correct candidate and breaking ties toward 3B; compare test accuracy and selected-model A100 latency with the global best-on-training choice.

follow_ups.title: Local latency cost-weight sweep
follow_ups.question: How does increasing a latency penalty change a learned router’s accuracy-latency trade-off?
follow_ups.method: Run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct locally on seed-42 MMLU and GSM8K samples of 40 training and 20 held-out questions per task, using greedy decoding and recording correctness and per-query A100 latency. For lambda values 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75, label training questions by maximizing correctness minus lambda times latency normalized by the training-set mean 7B latency, fit a TF-IDF/L2-logistic router, and compare held-out accuracy-latency points with the 3B-only and 7B-only choices.

follow_ups.title: Can an AutoMix-style verifier save calls?
follow_ups.question: Does a small model’s self-verification gate reduce larger-model calls while preserving answer quality?
follow_ups.method: On 40 fixed-seed test questions each from MMLU and GSM8K, run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct locally to draft an answer, then ask the same model to label the question-and-draft pair Correct or Incorrect using an AutoMix-style verifier prompt; send only Incorrect or malformed-verdict cases to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Score task-native accuracy against 3B-only and 7B-only baselines and count every draft, verification, and escalation call in generated tokens and A100 latency.

follow_ups.title: Is multi-round routing bottlenecked by controller size?
follow_ups.question: Does a 7B controller improve decomposition and aggregation over a 3B controller enough to justify its extra cost?
follow_ups.method: On 12 fixed-seed GSM8K test questions, compare direct greedy answers from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a multi-round pipeline in which either model decomposes each question into one or two self-contained subquestions and later aggregates the replies, while Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct answers every specialist call in both conditions. Score final answer matches and report accuracy, token use, and A100 latency with all decomposition, specialist, and aggregation calls counted.

follow_ups.title: Memory routing under a changing evidence budget
follow_ups.question: Does retrieval depth change which small model is most effective on long-conversation QA, and how does it affect input cost?
follow_ups.method: Select eight questions each from the LoCoMo and LongMemEval test sets with seed 42, split histories into speaker- and date-preserving turn pairs, embed questions and pairs with Contriever, and construct shared top-1 and top-5 retrieved contexts. Run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on every context using the paper’s memory prompts, then compare token-level F1, input-token counts, and A100 latency to see whether retrieval depth changes which model is preferable.

follow_ups.title: Do trend captions change time-series model strengths?
follow_ups.question: Does adding a text description to raw series values alter accuracy or the preferred model on the paper’s time-series reasoning skills?
follow_ups.method: Take two fixed-seed TSRBench questions from each of its seven skills, and have Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct write a one-paragraph, answer-free trend description from each numeric series. Run Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with the question and options under raw-values-only and raw-values-plus-shared-caption conditions; compare multiple-choice accuracy, error overlap, and A100 latency, charging caption-generation tokens only to the augmented condition.

follow_ups.title: Personalized routing on unseen personas
follow_ups.question: Does adding persona text improve held-out preference prediction for profiles not used to train the router?
follow_ups.method: Use 12 MT-Bench dialogue prompts and the ten persona descriptions printed in the paper; generate one persona-blind response per dialogue from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, reusing each response pair for all profiles. Have Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct locally judge each randomized pair using the dialogue and persona, train L2 TF-IDF preference selectors on eight complete profiles and test on the other two, and compare persona-plus-query, query-only, and global-choice predictions using 1/0.5/0 preference reward; report only agreement with this local judge, not human preference.

follow_ups.title: Per-node routing in a fixed chain agent
follow_ups.question: Does routing each node in a multi-agent chain help over using the 7B model at every node when the topology and call count are fixed?
follow_ups.method: Collect per-query correctness for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 20 training questions each from MMLU and GSM8K, and fit a TF-IDF/L2-logistic selector, breaking ties toward 3B; then run four disjoint held-out questions per task through a four-call Chain workflow with an initial answer, two verify-and-improve calls, and a final answer node. Let the selector choose a model independently from each full node prompt and compare with the identical chain using 7B at every call, scoring final task accuracy and total A100 latency and tokens.

follow_ups.title: Stability of routing supervision under sampling
follow_ups.question: How often does a single sampled completion give a different per-query model label from repeated completions?
follow_ups.method: For 30 held-out MMLU and 30 held-out GSM8K questions, generate three independent temperature-0.7 answers per question from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at fixed random seeds, and score every completion with the task metric. Compare each query’s winning-model label from the first draw with the label from the three-draw correctness rate, breaking ties toward 3B, and report label agreement and per-model accuracy variance across draws.

follow_ups.title: Learned routing versus fixed largest model on Generic tasks with a small pool
follow_ups.question: Do learned routers still outperform always selecting the largest model when the pool contains only 8B or smaller open models?
follow_ups.method: Run three 8B or smaller instruct models locally (for example Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-8B, Mistral-7B) on about 300 queries from MMLU, GSM8K and ARC-Challenge using the paper Appendix F benchmark prompts and native accuracy metrics. Build the query-model accuracy and token-cost matrix, train a kNN router over sentence embeddings with cross-validation to predict the best model per query, and compare its mean accuracy and total tokens to the fixed largest-parameter baseline.

follow_ups.title: No single router dominates across task families
follow_ups.question: Does the best-performing router change across knowledge QA, math reasoning and code generation?
follow_ups.method: Collect a 3-model 8B-or-smaller query-model matrix on three Generic subtasks (about 150 MMLU, 150 GSM8K, 100 MBPP) with Appendix F prompts and native metrics. Train and evaluate kNN, SVM classifier and Elo-style global-best routers by cross-validation within each subtask and compare which router wins per subtask and on average.

follow_ups.title: Router ranking reversal under increasing cost weight
follow_ups.question: Do router rankings reverse in favor of cheaper routers as the cost weight beta grows?
follow_ups.method: Reuse a small-pool query-model accuracy and token-cost matrix and assign per-token prices proportional to Table 9 to compute weighted reward alpha times perf minus beta times cost for beta from 0 to 0.8. Rank kNN, Elo global-best, smallest-model and largest-model policies at each beta and test whether the top-ranked router changes as beta increases.

follow_ups.title: Single-turn routing versus multi-round decompose-route-aggregate
follow_ups.question: Does multi-round decomposition and aggregation improve over single-turn routing once its extra calls are priced in?
follow_ups.method: On about 60 GSM8K and MATH queries collect single-turn responses from three 8B-or-smaller models and evaluate a cross-validated kNN router on accuracy and total tokens for the selected call only. For the same queries run a kNN-MultiRound baseline with an 8B base model using the Appendix F multi-round decomposition, specialist and aggregation prompts with at most 4 sub-queries, route each sub-query by kNN, price all decomposition, specialist and aggregation calls, and compare final accuracy and total cost to single-turn routing.

follow_ups.title: Sensitivity of multi-round routing to the base model
follow_ups.question: Does multi-round routing performance hinge on the capability of the base model that decomposes and aggregates?
follow_ups.method: Using about 60 GSM8K and MATH queries and fixed sub-query routing decisions, run the multi-round pipeline twice with two different 8B-or-smaller base models for decomposition and aggregation using Appendix F prompts. Compare final answer accuracy and total token cost across the two base models and against single-turn kNN routing.

follow_ups.title: User-conditioned versus user-agnostic routing with a small persona judge
follow_ups.question: Does conditioning routing decisions on user persona improve agreement with persona-conditioned preferences over user-agnostic routing?
follow_ups.method: Sample about 60 open-ended prompts from MT-Bench and 4 personas copied from Figure 10, generate answers with two 8B-or-smaller models, and judge each pair with an 8B instruct model using the Appendix F persona preference judge prompt with outputs 1, 2 or Tie. Train a persona-conditioned nearest-neighbor router on query plus persona embeddings and a persona-agnostic kNN router with cross-validation and compare agreement with held-out persona-judge preferences.

follow_ups.title: Cross-subtask generalization of text routers
follow_ups.question: Do routers trained on knowledge QA generalize to math and code queries or default to one model?
follow_ups.method: Build a 3-model 8B-or-smaller query-model matrix on about 200 MMLU knowledge queries and 200 GSM8K plus MBPP math and code queries with Appendix F prompts. Train kNN and SVM routers on knowledge only and evaluate on math and code and vice versa versus in-domain cross-validation, comparing accuracy and frequency of defaulting to a single model.

follow_ups.title: Routing with fixed retrieval when input-token cost dominates
follow_ups.question: Can routing beat single-model baselines on long-conversation QA when all candidates receive the same retrieved history and history tokens dominate cost?
follow_ups.method: Sample about 100 LoCoMo questions, split each history into turn pairs, retrieve top-5 pairs per query with a small Contriever encoder, and form Appendix F LoCoMo prompts so all candidates share identical evidence. Run three 8B-or-smaller models locally, score with token-level F1, record input and output tokens, and compare cross-validated kNN routing to fixed smallest and largest baselines on F1 and cost-weighted reward.

follow_ups.title: Per-node routing inside a multi-agent chain
follow_ups.question: Does routing each functional node independently improve final multi-agent accuracy over using one fixed model for all nodes?
follow_ups.method: Train a kNN router on about 150 Generic queries with three 8B-or-smaller models, then evaluate on about 30 held-out queries run through the Appendix F Chain topology where each of 4 agent prompts is routed independently versus all nodes using the fixed largest small model. Score final answers with the source task metric and compare mean accuracy and total tokens between per-node routed and fixed-model chains.

follow_ups.title: Greedy best-accuracy selection versus cost-aware cascade
follow_ups.question: Does a thresholded small-versus-large cascade achieve better cost-weighted reward than greedy accuracy-maximizing selection when cost matters?
follow_ups.method: From a 3-model 8B-or-smaller query-model matrix on Generic queries implement greedy argmax best-accuracy selection and a two-model Hybrid-LLM style cascade that predicts whether the smallest model suffices and thresholds the predicted gap. Compare weighted reward alpha times perf minus beta times cost at beta 0 and at high beta to test whether the cascade dominates greedy selection once cost is weighted.
